newsitem.title: USA: Dole repeats call to put off Bosnia elections.
newsitem.headline: Dole repeats call to put off Bosnia elections.

text.p: Republican presidential candididate Bob Dole on Thursday called again for President Bill Clinton to postpone planned elections in Bosnia, saying they would be a sham.

"These elections make a mockery of our principles and commitment to democracy," Dole said at a campaign appearance in this Ohio industrial city where the peace accords calling for the election were negotiated last year.
"There is still time for the president to postpone these elections. Many Americans, regardless of party, think it's a big mistake to pursue what would in effect be sham elections."
Dole, who lags Clinton by 15 to 20 percentage points in opinion polls, last week urged the president in a letter to put off the elections scheduled to take place on Sept. 14.

Voting for president and several legislative chambers is being run by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe. The Dayton treaty says the elections, which are supposed to reunify the ethnically divided country, should be "free and fair." But human rights workers say the voter registration process was plagued by abuses and nationalist authorities have stifled free speech and free movement.
Clinton has promised to bring some 20,000 American troops home after they finish their one-year mission in December as part of the NATO-led peace force.
